title: Image evidence: Hopewell-related Middle Woodland (about 200 BCE–500 CE, Ohio Valley)
summary: Middle Woodland communities in northern and eastern Kentucky tied to the wider Hopewell exchange network, building geometric earthworks such as Old Fort at the Portsmouth Group. Kentucky sites show Hopewell-style goods, though fewer than north of the Ohio.
displayNote: This picture is an AI illustration reconstructed from the available archaeological evidence for the Hopewell-related Middle Woodland period in Kentucky; details without direct evidence are informed guesses. AI illustration · Kentucky History Drive.

items.text: [Speculative] No open Kentucky skeletal study of build was confirmed; show ordinary build.
Copper and mica head ornaments are documented at Kentucky Hopewell-related sites (Wright-Greene, Robbins, Crigler); copper bicymbal ear spools at Amburgey.
[Speculative] Fabric technology likely continued Adena twining; specific Hopewell garments in Kentucky are not documented in these sources.
Copper breastplates/gorgets, solid bracelets, rings, ear spools; cut mica; marine shell beads; hooked-beak bird motifs.
Chert bladelets (Ohio Flint Ridge), platform pipes, copper celts; atlatl still in use.
Ohio River terrace in Greenup County: a square 13.5-acre earth enclosure with corners to the cardinal directions and long parallel embankments, part of the Portsmouth Group.

A person at the edge of a vast square earthen wall on an Ohio River terrace in morning mist, wearing copper ear spools, a copper breastplate and a cut-mica headpiece catching the light, holding a stone platform pipe. Broad river floodplain and the long parallel embankments behind; geometry emphasized to set it apart from Adena's round ridgetop mounds.
